messages:
mike: quick sync — we need a concrete plan for attributing per-request tokens/cost when a single user request can hit multiple models (routing, fallbacks, cache replays). currently billing just picks the final model and we lose the upstream token spend. this breaks per-team chargebacks and model-level cost dashboards.

tara: ugh yeah seen this with the reranker fallbacks. do you have a proposed schema?

mike: idea sketch: add a compact trace envelope that records the model hop sequence and token counts. minimal fields so it doesn't bloat telemetry: request_id, model_chain, tokens_per_model, cache_hit_mask, reason. embed as a header and as an optional enrichment at ingest. e.g.

```
X-RW-TRACE: request_id=req_12345; model_chain=[redwood/gpt-small:v1,open/llama-13b:v2]; tokens=[12,48]; cache=[true,false]; route_reason=[primary,capacity_fallback]
```

mike: runtime would emit this on every model call. ingest can either (A) persist the compact envelope (cheap) and later expand for billing jobs, or (B) explode into separate metered events per model. tradeoffs below.

jun: tradeoffs: (A) keeps ingest small but makes billing backfill/queries heavier — must rehydrate envelopes for time-series and joins. (B) increases SPM at ingest and the cardinality of metrics/tags (model_id as tag) which spikes storage.

lina: also need to consider caching: replayed tokens shouldn't double-bill. cache mask + original_token_count should be enough to dedupe, but we need canonical request id across proxies. how robust is request_id propagation today?

mike: good point. implementor note: request_id should be generated at edge and carried through all internal calls. if absent, runtime should generate a guid and mark origin="internal". we'll add validation in ingest to drop envelopes missing stable origin.

tara: what about sampling? for high-volume customers we can't keep full envelopes for every request. propose heuristic: sample 1% full envelopes, 100% compact envelopes (one-liner), and compute expected per-model splits via extrapolation. billing needs deterministic sampling for audits.

jun: deterministic sampling = hash(request_id)%100 < sample_rate. keep sample_rate in tenant config. OK. also we should emit a sampled=true flag in header so downstream knows why detailed data missing.

mike: ops concerns: if we persist exploded per-model events (option B) we must ensure low-cardinality tags only: model_family instead of model_full_version, and then have a separate low-traffic table mapping model_version -> owner for chargebacks. avoids hot cardinality on time-series index.

lina: alternative: keep per-model micro-events in a separate append-only billing stream (cold path). cheap to write, but only materialized in billing jobs. this reduces pressure on the observability TSDB.

obs-bot: deploy-bot: noted. opened infra ticket INF-2234 to add X-RW-TRACE header passthrough and sampling flags to runtime.

mike: next steps: 1) finalize header spec (short names), 2) runtime PR to emit on model calls, 3) ingest change to persist compact envelope + sampled detailed envelopes, 4) billing job to rehydrate and compute per-model token/cost. i'll draft RFC with examples and cost estimate. anyone want to take the RFC draft? @tara? :coffee:
